title: Unmasking Nationality Bias: A Study of Human Perception of Nationalities in AI-Generated Articles
benchmark_measurement: The study measured nationality bias in AI-generated text through human evaluation. As part of this, it indirectly measured religious bias by observing how AI models associate specific nationalities (e.g., from Tunisia, Libya) with religious terms like 'islamist' and 'islamic' as part of a broader pattern of stereotyping.
findings: The study found that the AI model, GPT-2, tended to amplify stereotypes for certain nationalities. In the context of religion, it specifically used adjectives like 'islamic' and 'islamist' when generating text about countries like Libya and Tunisia, which was part of a larger pattern of generating more negative and narrowly-themed content for these nations compared to human-written articles.
